newsitem.title: SPAIN: Michelin sees slight gain from dollar rise.
newsitem.headline: Michelin sees slight gain from dollar rise.

text.p: Michelin finance director Eric Bourdais de Charbonniere said he believed the dollar's recent rise against the French franc was slightly advantageous, on balance, for the French tyremaker.
He said on the one hand, the dollar's gains translate into higher earnings in francs from activities in the United States and countries with currencies linked to the dollar.

But on the other hand, the dollar's advance pushes up raw materials prices indexed to the dollar, Bourdais de Charbonniere told reporters on a tour of Michelin's tyre testing facility in the southern Spanish town of Almeria.

"The equation shows these factors balance each other out, but I conclude there remains an advantage to a stronger dollar because we can pass part of the raw materials cost increase on to tyre prices," he said.
Michelin's raw materials costs weakened slightly in 1996, he said, but if the dollar rose further, as he expected it would, the company would have to consider raising tyre prices.

"I think the dollar's rise isn't finished," he said, adding that the difference between the strength of the U.S. and European economies justified a widening in the gap between their respective interest rates.

He said the dollar's strength was "less positive" for the group's debt -- 23.2 billion francs at the end of June 1996 -- than for its results. Michelin's debt exposure in dollars was roughly equivalent to the proportion of sales in dollars, or around 35 percent, he said. ($1 = 5.56 francs)
